intended_use: Detailed self-study reading materials aligned to the role/topic inventory used for the 12,000-question MCQ/MSQ bank.

schema.topics: Each topic module contains learning objectives, detailed reading notes, practice tasks, pitfalls, and mastery checks.
schema.source_question_count: Number of questions in the original bank for this role/topic.

roles.role_mission: build image and video systems for detection, segmentation, recognition, OCR, tracking, and visual understanding
roles.quality_bar: vision models generalize across scenes, cameras, lighting, domains, and deployment constraints without hidden leakage
reading_strategy: Read the first pass for vocabulary and assumptions.
Read the second pass by building a small artifact for each topic.
For every topic, write one failure mode, one diagnostic, one stakeholder caveat, and one production or governance implication.
Treat medium questions as application checks and hard questions as failure-mode, tradeoff, and design-reasoning checks.

topics.learning_objective: Master train-test contamination through near duplicates well enough to apply it in the Computer Vision Engineer role: define the assumptions, choose the right method or design, detect subtle failure modes, and explain tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
topics.overview: This module treats train-test contamination through near duplicates as a medium-to-hard job skill for a Computer Vision Engineer. Read it through the lens of visual data quality, spatial metrics, domain shift, and deployment constraints. The goal is not memorization; it is being able to reason from first principles, audit edge cases, and produce artifacts such as vision training pipeline, annotation protocol, model card.
topics.role_application: For a Computer Vision Engineer, train-test contamination through near duplicates matters because the role's mission is to build image and video systems for detection, segmentation, recognition, OCR, tracking, and visual understanding. The expected quality bar is that vision models generalize across scenes, cameras, lighting, domains, and deployment constraints without hidden leakage. When answering interview questions or doing project work, connect train-test contamination through near duplicates to a real artifact and a measurable decision.
reading_path: Define the exact problem statement for train-test contamination through near duplicates: inputs, outputs, users, decision point, and failure cost.
Write the assumptions that must hold for train-test contamination through near duplicates to be valid in a realistic Computer Vision Engineer workflow.
Study the mechanics using a small worked example, then deliberately break the example with edge cases.
Map diagnostics and quality checks to concrete artifacts: tests, dashboards, evaluation tables, runbooks, or decision memos.
Summarize the tradeoffs in one page: when to use the technique, when not to use it, and how to monitor it after launch.

topics.learning_objective: Master eval set contamination well enough to apply it in the Speech/Audio AI Engineer role: define the assumptions, choose the right method or design, detect subtle failure modes, and explain tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
topics.overview: This module treats eval set contamination as a medium-to-hard job skill for a Speech/Audio AI Engineer. Read it through the lens of signal processing, sequence modeling, streaming constraints, and human perception. The goal is not memorization; it is being able to reason from first principles, audit edge cases, and produce artifacts such as ASR/TTS model, audio evaluation set, latency profile.
topics.role_application: For a Speech/Audio AI Engineer, eval set contamination matters because the role's mission is to build speech and audio systems for ASR, TTS, diarization, verification, enhancement, keyword spotting, and audio event understanding. The expected quality bar is that audio models handle noise, accents, latency, privacy, and subjective quality with measurable error decomposition. When answering interview questions or doing project work, connect eval set contamination to a real artifact and a measurable decision.
reading_path: Define the exact problem statement for eval set contamination: inputs, outputs, users, decision point, and failure cost.
Write the assumptions that must hold for eval set contamination to be valid in a realistic Speech/Audio AI Engineer workflow.
Study the mechanics using a small worked example, then deliberately break the example with edge cases.
Map diagnostics and quality checks to concrete artifacts: tests, dashboards, evaluation tables, runbooks, or decision memos.
Summarize the tradeoffs in one page: when to use the technique, when not to use it, and how to monitor it after launch.

topics.learning_objective: Master real-time constraints well enough to apply it in the Robotics/Reinforcement Learning Engineer role: define the assumptions, choose the right method or design, detect subtle failure modes, and explain tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

topics.learning_objective: Master human-robot interaction well enough to apply it in the Robotics/Reinforcement Learning Engineer role: define the assumptions, choose the right method or design, detect subtle failure modes, and explain tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
topics.overview: This module treats human-robot interaction as a medium-to-hard job skill for a Robotics/Reinforcement Learning Engineer. topics.role_application: For a Robotics/Reinforcement Learning Engineer, human-robot interaction matters because the role's mission is to build agents and robots that act safely under uncertainty using perception, planning, control, imitation, and reinforcement learning. When answering interview questions or doing project work, connect human-robot interaction to a real artifact and a measurable decision.

Summarize the tradeoffs in one page: when to use the technique, when not to use it, and how to monitor it after launch.

Introduce two edge cases that would mislead a superficial solution for risk-sensitive objectives.
Write the checks or metrics that would catch those edge cases before a decision, launch, or handoff.
Prepare a short stakeholder explanation that includes assumptions, tradeoffs, and residual risk.
practice_lab.deliverable: A concise artifact proving you can apply risk-sensitive objectives: one table, diagram, query, evaluation report, runbook, or decision memo plus a paragraph of caveats.

practice_drills: formulate an MDP/POMDP for a robot task
design a sim-to-real validation ladder
write safety constraints and rollback triggers for policy rollout
common_pitfalls: reward shaping that teaches the wrong behavior
assuming simulation success transfers to hardware unchanged
using off-policy data outside its support
ignoring real-time latency and actuator constraints
mastery_check: Explain risk-sensitive objectives without using buzzwords, including the assumptions and what can go wrong.
Given a messy scenario, choose an appropriate method or design for risk-sensitive objectives and justify it against at least two alternatives.
Design validation checks that would detect silent failure or misleading success for risk-sensitive objectives.
Communicate the conclusion with uncertainty, limitations, and a next action.
assessment_prompts: What is the most dangerous hidden assumption in a typical use of risk-sensitive objectives, and how would you test it?
How would your answer change if data volume, latency, privacy, or cost constraints became 10x tighter?
What metric or diagnostic would you distrust most for risk-sensitive objectives, and what companion evidence would you require?
